about:
Low Energy is a COVID era collaboration with Denver based progressive trance producer, Black Wands, who is also my cousin Alex.

When we were teenagers, I went to see his punk band rehearse. I remember someone got blood on the snare drum, and I thought it was so cool. This was back when Alex played a banana-yellow Fender Supersonic. Before he got into electronic music. I remember falling asleep in his basement, dreaming of buying my first guitar.

In 2021, I was really into the Weeknd album, After Hours. I had just bought my first synthesizer to celebrate starting a new job, and I was hungry to explore what it could do.*

Stuck inside the house, I was feeling restless, and things were just off between me and my partner. We felt the weight of the world on our relationship, and being stuck inside only amplified that. This song became an outlet for all of that restless energy; A vicarious dance party; A way to break the confinement.

I'd get on a zoom call with Alex, and we'd work on the song for hours. I'd record bits and send them over, then he'd send back his edits. Eventually we got in the same room together, and that's when things really got going. He had this tiny keyboard in his home studio. It didn't have enough keys to play the melody I wrote, so I had to take the last note and flip it over the edge of the instrument to the octave above (3:36). It gave the part this insane energy that I never would have captured at home.**

I had never really worked on dance music before, and Alex had never really done pop. But I think artists do their best work when they're juuust outside of their comfort zone. It's where the joy of discovery is the strongest and the force of habit fades.

Where magic happens.


* Technically I didn't have the job yet, but I saw a bargain and I went for it

** I recorded the vocals with Robert Trusko in his home studio in Dallas. He's got a one room in-law unit with nothing but a bookshelf separating the studio from the bed. I remember laying down, listening to him work as he stacked up my vocals in the bridge.
